verses.text: Jesus entered Jericho and was walking through town.
There was a man named Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector—and he was loaded.
He was trying to catch a look at Jesus, but the crowd was in the way. Zacchaeus was short, so he couldn’t see over them.
He ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree, because Jesus was about to pass that way.
When Jesus reached the spot, he looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry down! I need to stay at your place today.”
Zacchaeus hurried down and welcomed him with joy.
Everybody saw it and started grumbling: “He’s gone to stay with a sinner?”
Zacchaeus stood up and told the Lord, “Look, Lord, I’m giving half my stuff to the poor. And if I’ve cheated anybody, I’ll pay them back four times over.”
Jesus said, “Today, salvation has come to this house. This man is Abraham’s son too.”
“The Son of Man came to look for and save the people who were lost.”
While they were listening, Jesus told another story because he was near Jerusalem, and they thought God’s Kingdom was about to show up right away.
He said, “A nobleman went to a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself and then come back.”
“He called ten of his servants, gave them ten minas, and said, ‘Do business with this until I get back.’”
“But his people hated him. They sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We don’t want this man ruling over us.’”
“When he came back as king, he called in the servants he’d given the money to. He wanted to find out what they’d earned.”
“The first one came in and said, ‘Sir, your mina earned ten more.’”
“The king said, ‘Well done, good servant! You were faithful with a little, so now you’re in charge of ten cities.’”
“The second came in and said, ‘Sir, your mina earned five more.’”
“The king told him, ‘You’re in charge of five cities.’”
“Another servant came in and said, ‘Sir, here’s your mina. I kept it wrapped up in a cloth,”
“‘because I was scared of you. You’re a tough man: you take what you didn’t put down and harvest what you didn’t plant.’”
“The king said, ‘I’ll judge you by your own words, you wicked servant! You knew I was tough, taking what I didn’t put down and harvesting what I didn’t plant.”
“‘So why didn’t you put my money in the bank? Then when I came back, I could’ve collected it with interest.’”
“He told the people standing there, ‘Take that mina away from him and give it to the one who has ten.’”
“They said, ‘Sir, he already has ten minas!’”
“‘I’m telling you, everyone who has will get more. But whoever has nothing—even what they have will be taken away.”
“‘And bring my enemies here—the ones who didn’t want me ruling over them—and kill them in front of me.’”
After telling them this, Jesus went on ahead, heading up to Jerusalem.
When he came near Bethphage and Bethany, by the hill called the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples.
He said, “Go to the village over there. As you enter, you’ll find a young donkey tied up, one nobody has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.”
“If anyone asks, ‘Why are you untying it?’ tell them, ‘The Lord needs it.’”
The two disciples went and found it just as Jesus had told them.
As they were untying the donkey, its owners asked, “Why are you untying it?”
They said, “The Lord needs it.”
They brought it to Jesus, threw their cloaks over the donkey, and sat Jesus on it.
As he rode along, people spread their cloaks on the road.
When he was coming down the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of disciples started celebrating and praising God loudly for all the miracles they’d seen. 🙌
They shouted, “Blessed is the King who comes in the Lord’s name! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”
Some Pharisees in the crowd said to Jesus, “Teacher, tell your disciples to stop!”
He answered, “I’m telling you, if they went quiet, the stones would start shouting.”
When Jesus came closer and saw the city, he wept over it.
He said, “If only you’d understood today what could bring you peace! But now it’s hidden from your eyes.”
“The days are coming when your enemies will build a barricade around you. They’ll surround you, close in from every side,”
“and crush you and your children to the ground. They won’t leave one stone on top of another, because you didn’t recognize the time God came to you.”
Jesus entered the temple and began driving out the people buying and selling there.
He said, “The Scriptures say, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’ but you’ve turned it into a ‘hideout for robbers’!”
Jesus taught in the temple every day. The chief priests, the law teachers, and the leaders of the people were looking for a way to kill him.
But they couldn’t find a way to do it, because all the people were hanging on every word he said.
